anna: Heads-up — profiler showed persistent small-prefix KV entries being created across requests for longctx workloads. Memory climbs steadily and eviction churn spikes after ~15–20k tokens. I dumped a few samples and eviction logs.

derek: can you paste the sample keys / eviction logs?

anna: sure, sample excerpt:
```
KV_CREATE tenant=acme session=abcd-123 prefix="What is the user's" pos=12 key=sha256(....aa)
KV_CREATE tenant=acme session=efgh-999 prefix="What is the user's" pos=13 key=sha256(....ab)
KV_CREATE tenant=other session=zz11 prefix="What is the user's" pos=12 key=sha256(....ac)
EVICT tenant=acme freed_pages=2 fragmentation=0.31
EVICT tenant=acme freed_pages=1 fragmentation=0.33
```

rafi: looks like session id is in the key derivation, which prevents cross-request reuse when prefix is identical but session differs. prolif of near-identical keys -> fragmentation + poor locality.

derek: exact. current derivation is `sha256(session_id + ':' + prefix + ':' + pos)` so every new session makes distinct keys even for same tenant/prompt.

anna: we tried forcing sticky-session reuse earlier but that broke privacy constraints for some enterprise tenants. need a pattern that allows reuse for safe prefixes while avoiding cross-tenant leakage.

infra-bot: cache_stats: evictions_per_sec=118, free_pages_pct=21.8, residency_avg_ms=1423, fragmentation_ratio=0.34

derek: proposal — separate namespaces: tenant-scoped canonical prefix keys + ephemeral session delta. Key derivation:
```
# old
key = sha256(f"{session_id}:{prefix}:{pos}")

# proposal
canonical_key = sha256(f"T:{tenant_id}:{normalize(prefix)}:{pos}")
ephemeral_key = sha256(f"S:{session_id}:{pos}")
```
This lets identical prefixes across sessions reuse canonical entries, while ephemeral per-session keys capture mutable state.

rafi: normalize(prefix) should collapse whitespace, redact user tokens, and truncate to first N tokens to avoid explosion. Also we should include a tenant salt to prevent accidental cross-tenant collisions.

anna: rolled a small canary patch for acme-only: switched to canonical_key derivation + per-tenant LRU cap. initial results: reuse hit-rate jumped 0.18 -> 0.62, memory growth plateaued at ~8% lower than baseline, eviction latency median reduced 37ms -> 12ms. however we saw a correctness regression in 1/500k requests where tenant-specific tokenization caused prefix equivalence to be incorrect.

derek: we need a safety gating rule: only canonicalize prefixes that pass a sanitizer (no tenant-unique tokens, no user PII). If sanitizer fails, fallback to old session-scoped key.

rafi: also add a residency time heuristic: only promote a prefix into tenant-canonical namespace after it's been observed X times across Y distinct sessions to avoid premature promotion of noisy prefixes.

derek: agree. add metrics to console: "canonical_promotions", "promotion_failures", "tenant_lru_evictions". Will add gating in rollout plan.

anna: quick iteration note — when we moved normalization to be aggressive (strip punctuation + lower), a few prompts changed meaning for role-based templating. So sanitizer needs to be configurable per-tenant. config example:
```
tenant_config["acme"].sanitize = { redact_emails: true, keep_case_for_tokens: ["{{ROLE}}"] }
```

infra-bot: canary metrics (24h): canonical_promotions=2.1k, promotion_failures=45, reuse_improvement=3.4x, error_inc=+0.02% (mostly template edgecases)

rafi: sounds promising. next steps: 1) RFC with safe-sanitizer design + testcases, 2) add per-tenant promotion thresholds, 3) add automated regression tests with role/template variations, 4) phased rollout with monitoring alerts for promotion_failures > threshold.

derek: I'll open the GH issue and add the perf numbers + example logs. tagging @infra to help with dashboard metrics.

anna: thanks — will own the RFC and test harness. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-canary acme -> success 2950012399

anna: FYI — one more observation: kernel selection for quantized kernels changed throughput slightly when we promoted canonicalized prefixes; batching improved because more requests hit cold cache entries. so the change had a nice side-effect on batching heuristics too.

derek: neat. that strengthens the case. anyone opposed to merging the RFC after tests?

rafi: no objections. I'll help write tests.

anna: ok, filing notes in the ticket and linking the canary dashboard.
